newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Beach finds new oil zone in US well.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Beach finds new oil zone in US well.

text.p: Beach Petroleum NL said on Monday the discovery of oil in a new reservoir formation at its South Burbank operation in Osage County, Oklahoma, had significantly extended the scope for further oil production.
Beach chief executive Reg Nelson said in a statement that drilling had recommenced at its J-14 well on February 13.

"Drilling is being conducted using foam and has resulted in continuous and steady oil shows within the Mississippi Limestone, with 30 BBL (barrels) of oil having being collected during this phase of drilling," he said.
The well had reached a depth of 905 metres on February 15 and was still showing strong oil recovery, he said.
"This discovery in a new reservoir formation beneath the (Mississippi) Chat has significantly extended the scope for further oil production from the South Burbank Unit," he said.
Oil accumulations appeared to be stratigraphically controlled and may cover a large portion of the leased area, he said.
It was now planned to drill to a total depth of 927 metres with a possible further extension to test the deeper Simpson Formation, he said.
Nelson said casing had been set to the base of the Mississippi Chat in which a potential production zone from 852.2 to 856.8 metres had been identified.
